turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I came in because I just keep losing chunks of time every day. I work on computers, so I end up constantly re-reading emails and texts, or reopening folders I just closed. And then, before I can even leave the house or actually start my work, I find myself mentally replaying conversations over and over. It's... well, it's like I'm trying to prove to myself that I didn't make some serious mistake somewhere. It's just getting really hard to manage.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes repetitive checking behaviors (re-reading emails/texts, reopening folders) and mental acts (replaying conversations repeatedly to ensure no mistake was made) that consume significant time.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel driven to mentally replay these conversations to prevent something bad from happening, or do you worry that something bad will happen if you don’t get them ‘right’ in your mind?

Well, like I was saying a minute ago, it's really about trying to prove to myself that I didn't make a serious mistake. I don't know if I'm picturing a specific disaster happening, it's just... I have to be absolutely sure I didn't mess up somewhere. 

So I get stuck. I end up losing all that time just going back over things—re-reading the same emails, reopening the work folders I just looked at, or running those conversations through my head again and again before I can even leave the house. I just can't seem to move on until I feel sure I didn't do something wrong.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes engaging in repetitive checking behaviors (re-reading emails, reopening folders) and mental acts (running conversations through their head repeatedly) driven by the need to be sure they didn't make a mistake before they can move on.

turns.doctor_question: Are these conversations you replay in your mind things that you don’t really want to think about, but they keep coming up and bothering you, even when you try not to focus on them?

Yes, exactly. I really don't want to be thinking about them. I'll be right in the middle of trying to work through a system design, or maybe preparing a lesson, and... well, this thought just keeps barging in. 

It'll be something like worrying I sent the wrong message to my ex-wife, or that I mishandled some family photos, or even that I let someone in the community down somehow. I try to push it away because I know I’ve already been over it, but... I just can’t seem to let it pass. It just keeps coming up and interrupting me until I focus on it again.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly confirms experiencing persistent, intrusive, and unwanted thoughts that they try to suppress or push away but cannot let pass, meeting criteria for obsessions.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that you have to perform these mental reviews or behaviors in a certain way, or a certain number of times, to feel that everything is okay or to prevent something bad from happening?

No, not really. I don't have a specific number of times I have to do it, like counting or anything. And I don't think I do it in a particular way, either. 

It's... well, it's really just about doing it until I feel sure. I just keep re-reading the email or replaying the conversation until that nagging feeling of doubt finally goes away, however long that takes. But it's not a set number or a specific routine.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient confirms engaging in compulsions by stating that they repeatedly re-read emails and replay conversations to relieve a persistent feeling of doubt until they feel sure.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel anxious or upset if you’re not able to go back and check or replay these things in your mind?

It's like this tight, uncomfortable feeling that just builds and builds. I get really agitated because my brain is telling me I need to figure it out right that second, and if I can't, it's almost impossible to focus on anything else.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever have thoughts, images, or urges that come into your mind that feel intrusive and unwanted, and that you try to get rid of or neutralize in some way?

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel driven to perform these mental reviews in a specific, ritualized way, such as needing to remember every detail perfectly or only moving on after you've reviewed the conversation 'just right' in your mind?
